question: The radius of the circle is 8 cm. The distance of a point lying outside the circle from the centre is 17 cm. The length of the tangent drawn from the outside point to the circle is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A tangent to a circle makes a 90° angle with the radius at the point of contact, forming a right-angled triangle.

Given the hypotenuse (distance from centre) is 17 cm and one side (radius) is 8 cm.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17), the length of the tangent must be 15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**
